t: The lake that disappeared from the map before it disappeared from the ground
s: A 43-acre irrigation tank still exists in the revenue records. On the ground, half of it is now a layout with numbered plots. Villagers say the change happened over four monsoons, and nobody was told.
b: This is a sample story so you can see how the website looks. Delete this file once you publish your own reports. The first thing you notice is that the water has an edge to it now. Not the soft, uncertain edge of a tank that fills and empties with the season, but a straight line, cut by a compound wall that runs for almost four hundred metres along what used to be the northern bund. Behind the wall, the ground has been levelled and marked into rectangles. Small cement pillars carry numbers painted in red. Plot 14. Plot 15. Plot 16. t: Six villages, one bus, and a school day that starts at 5.40 in the morning
s: The route was cut from four services to one during the pandemic and never restored. Children now leave home in the dark to reach a school eleven kilometres away.
b: Sample story — delete this file once your own reports are up. At twenty to six the road is still blue-dark, and there are eleven children standing at the junction with their bags already on their backs. The bus is due at 5.55. It is usually late. If it does not come at all, which happens perhaps twice a month, they walk to the main road and wait for a share auto, and they reach school after the second period has started. t: The town says it segregates waste. Its own dump yard says otherwise
s: Municipal records claim 78 percent source segregation. Four hours at the dump yard, watching what actually arrives, tells a different story.
b: Sample story — delete this file once your own reports are up. The claim is on a board at the municipal office, painted in green: 78% source segregation achieved. It has been there long enough for the paint to fade at one corner. Segregation means households separating wet waste from dry waste before it is collected. It is the single thing that decides whether a town's garbage becomes compost and recyclables, or becomes a hill. t: How to file an RTI in Tamil Nadu — and what to do when they do not reply
s: You do not need a lawyer, a format, or a reason. You need ten rupees, one address, and the patience to use the appeal that almost nobody uses.
b: Sample story — delete this file once your own reports are up. Most people who give up on the Right to Information Act give up at the same place: the silence after the first application. That silence is not the end of the process. It is a specific stage of it, with a specific remedy, and the remedy is free. Filing it Write it on plain paper. There is no official form for Tamil Nadu. t: Three roads, three contractors, one estimate — a ward's paperwork does not add up
s: Work orders obtained under RTI show identical estimates for roads of very different lengths, issued within nine days of each other.
b: Sample story — delete this file once your own reports are up. The three roads are not alike. One is 410 metres. One is 260 metres. One is 690 metres. Walking them takes an afternoon, and it is obvious from the walking alone that they are not the same job. The estimates say they cost the same.
